questions.title: Levels of structural organization of the body
questions.subject: fnd
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Physiology > Homeostasis > Levels of Organization
questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the hierarchical levels of structural organization of the human body, from simplest to most complex?

options.A: Cells, tissues, chemicals, organs, systems, whole body
options.B: Chemicals, cells, tissues, organs, systems, whole body
options.C: Chemicals, organs, cells, tissues, systems, whole body
options.D: Tissues, cells, chemicals, systems, organs, whole body

explanations.A: Incorrect. This places cells before chemicals, but chemicals (atoms and molecules) are the most basic level and must precede cells, which are themselves built from chemicals.
explanations.B: Correct. The body is organized in ascending order of complexity as chemicals, cells, tissues, organs, systems, and finally the whole body, with each level built from, and dependent on, the level immediately below it. Each level in this hierarchy is built from, and depends on, the level immediately below it, which is why the order can never be scrambled.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This places organs before cells and tissues, but an organ is composed of two or more tissue types, and a tissue is composed of cells, so organs cannot precede either in the hierarchy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This scrambles the order further, placing tissues first and chemicals in the middle; chemicals must be the foundational first level, since cells themselves are built from chemical components.

questions.learning_objective: State the correct ascending order of structural organization: chemicals, cells, tissues, organs, systems, whole body.
